narrative.overview:
Relay is a job control deck, not a chat app. A request enters as an INPUT field, the agent's work appears as operation records with return codes, and a persistent Operator Information Area tells the truth about runtime state along the bottom edge. The 3270 field grammar is deliberate: reversed label bars, fixed-width data, square annunciator lamps, and no decorative chrome between the operator and the machine.

The surface is flat blue-black in dark mode and cool printout grey in light mode, but the grammar is identical in both. Panels are separated by 1px rules and small tonal steps, never by drop shadows. Color is functional: turquoise means interactive, green means ready or complete, amber means attention or pending, red means alarm or denied. Nothing else gets a hue.

The console refuses the category defaults: no centered hero floating over cards, no speech bubbles, no gradient glass, no pill-shaped chips, no rounded panels. Density is the point. A solo developer should be able to watch the reasoning turn, the translator, the gates, the tool result, and the context budget without opening a dialog or decoding a bubble.
keyCharacteristics: Square geometry: every surface has 0 radius; the spinner is the only circle.
1px rules and tonal steps carry structure; shadows belong only to overlays.
Reversed ink label bars anchor the field grammar.
Exactly four signal hues, each with one meaning, in both themes.
Monospace for every label, number, path, tool name, and status token.
The 26px OIA status line is always visible and never decorative.
Light theme is a printout of the same console, not a separate design.

rules.name: The Four-Lamp Rule
rules.body: Turquoise is interactive, green is ready, amber is attention, red is alarm. There is no fifth hue and no decorative use of these four. Reach for weight, a rule, or a reversed bar before color.

rules.name: The Two-Knob Rule
rules.body: The operator controls exactly two colors: a base and an accent. Every surface, rule, and text tone derives from them via color-mix. Never hardcode a palette hex in a theme-following component.

rules.name: The Printout Mirror Rule
rules.body: Light mode keeps the same hue assignments and contrast roles as dark mode. It does not introduce a second accent, warm the paper, or invert signal meanings.

rules.name: The 12px Floor
rules.body: No functional text renders below 12px, including badges, timestamps, table headers, status segments, and helper copy.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number, path, tool name, and status token is monospace with tabular figures so streaming counts do not jitter.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface sits in normal document flow, it has no shadow. Add a rule or a tonal step instead. Shadows mean the element is temporarily above the deck.

rules.name: The Rule-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Use a 1px border to separate two surfaces before considering any other treatment.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Every panel, control, badge, chip, card, dialog, and avatar is 0 radius. The loading spinner is the only circle.

rules.name: The Truthful OIA Rule
rules.body: The status line reflects real runtime state at every breakpoint. It is never filled with marketing copy or decorative telemetry.

dos: Do separate surfaces with a 1px rule or a tonal step first.
Do put field labels in reversed ink bars at 12px mono uppercase.
Do set numbers, paths, tool names, and status tokens in tabular monospace.
Do keep one primary turquoise action per surface.
Do keep the OIA line visible at every breakpoint, including mobile.
Do derive new colors from the operator's base and accent.
donts: Don't round a corner; the spinner is the only circle.
Don't put a shadow on a resting panel, card, or nav row.
Don't use turquoise, green, amber, or red decoratively.
Don't render functional text below 12px or track labels wider than 0.07em.
Don't add gradients, glass, glow, or a second accent hue.
Don't hide the pipeline, approvals, or run status behind a routine dialog.
Don't introduce a new signal hue for a new state.
